sections.h2: Who bills property tax in Fayetteville, NC?
sections.html:
One county office, Cumberland Tax Administration, sets the assessed value of a Fayetteville house and also mails the bill and takes the payment. The City of Fayetteville adopts its own rate, but the county puts both levies on a single bill.

The office sits at 117 Dick Street, Room 530, Fayetteville, NC 28301, and answers at 910-678-7507. Mail goes to Cumberland Tax Administration, PO Box 449, Fayetteville NC 28302. Most owners see the Fayetteville city rate, the county rate and any city fees stacked on one statement, which is why a closing agent asks for the parcel number before quoting a payoff.

The Census Bureau puts Fayetteville at 209,120 people on July 1, 2025, across 148.26 square miles of land. The county page on local history gives 661 square miles for the county and records that Campbellton took the name Fayetteville in 1783 and that a fire in 1831 burned most of the town. The county history traces the base now called Fort Bragg to a 1918 artillery camp.

sections.h2: What rates and fees show up on a Fayetteville tax bill?
sections.html:
A Fayetteville bill combines a county rate of 49.9 cents per $100 of value with a city rate of 44.95 cents per $100, plus flat fees for trash and stormwater.

The county's rate page covers the 2026 tax bills (fiscal year 2027). It prints each levy as a decimal, and the combined figure for the city is 0.9485. Unincorporated owners pay a different mix, including a fire district charge and a recreation rate, so a house just outside the city line is billed differently from one inside it.

Fayetteville levies as printed by Cumberland County for 2026 tax bills (source: county Tax Rates page)

The stormwater tiers turn on impervious surface. Tier 1 is under 2,500 square feet, tier 2 runs from 2,501 to 4,800 square feet, and tier 3 is anything larger. Two rules to remember:

  • The combined rate on the page leaves out stormwater, solid waste, refuse, recycling and transit charges, so the real bill is higher than the rate alone suggests.
  • Parcels inside the revitalization district carry an added levy on top of the city rate.

sections.h2: What is the payment calendar for a Fayetteville bill?
sections.html:
Cumberland bills carry a September 1 due date, and the rate page puts the interest-free cutoff at January 5.

G.S. 105-360 sets that rhythm for the whole state. A payment that arrives before January 6 costs only the face amount. From January 6 until February 1, a 2 percent charge applies, and after that the account gains three-fourths of one percent for every month or part of a month. The county's 2025 revaluation calendar listed August for mailing that year's bills, and owners who cannot pay all at once can phone 910-678-7507 to arrange installments.

Ask the closing attorney whether the payoff covers the current-year bill. Because the lien follows the parcel to its next owner, an unpaid balance does not vanish at the deed. The lien rules are in G.S. 105-355.

sections.h2: How did the 2025 revaluation change Fayetteville assessments?
sections.html:
Every parcel in Cumberland County was reappraised to its January 1, 2025 market value, replacing values set in 2017.

The county's revaluation page says the last prior reappraisal took effect January 1, 2017, and cites the state requirement that counties reappraise at least once every eight years. It describes the goal as equity between properties, with no intent to raise or lower total tax. Notices went out February 21, 2025, and the new rates took effect July 1, 2025 once the county and the city adopted their budgets.

Relief approvals carry over. The county's page says previously approved tax relief applications stay valid and nobody has to refile after revaluation. Its FAQ adds that an exemption's approval stays in place while the billed amount moves with the new value.

sections.h2: Where do I send a challenge to my Fayetteville value?
sections.html:
Send an informal Request for Review to Tax Administration first, and carry any open dispute to the Board of Equalization and Review.

  • Informal review: submit online, by mail, by email, at Room 530 of the county courthouse at 117 Dick Street, or through the secure drop box in the back parking lot. Attach evidence such as comparable sales.
  • Deadline: the county's page lists February 5, 2027 for informal appeals on the 2027 tax year, and a decision letter follows around April 2027.
  • Board hearing: the 2026 Board of Equalization and Review adjourned May 20, 2026, which closed that year's window.
  • Further appeal: the state Property Tax Commission takes a written notice filed inside 30 days of the board's mailed ruling (G.S. 105-290).

Informal requests by mail go to Cumberland Tax Administration, Attn: Real Estate Assessment, PO Box 449, Fayetteville NC 28302. Give a working phone number and mailing address, because an appraiser may schedule a visit to the house.

sections.h2: Can a Fayetteville homeowner shrink the bill with a relief program?
sections.html:
Three state programs exist, and each owner can draw from just one: a senior or disability exclusion, a disabled veteran exclusion and a circuit breaker cap.

  • Senior or disabled owners with 2026 income at or below $38,800 shield at least $25,000 of value, or half the value when that figure is larger (G.S. 105-277.1).
  • Disabled veterans shield $45,000 of value, regardless of age or income (G.S. 105-277.1C).
  • The circuit breaker holds the bill to 4 percent of income, or 5 percent for income between $38,800 and $58,200, and defers the remainder as a lien (G.S. 105-277.1B).

Apply on Form AV-9 at the county assessor's office, preferably in January and no later than June 1 before the tax year. Cumberland says earlier approvals remain valid after the 2025 revaluation. Selling the house ends a circuit breaker deferral, and three years of deferred tax then fall due.

sections.h2: What if I list or sell a Fayetteville house while tax is unpaid?
sections.html:
The balance is cleared from sale proceeds at the table, since the lien attached to the parcel on the January 1 listing date.

Get a written payoff from the county that includes interest and city fees, then pass it to the closing attorney. A bill left unpaid after January 5 can end in a court foreclosure of the lien. G.S. 105-374 describes a public auction at the courthouse door, and a person redeeming before confirmation pays taxes, penalties, interest and costs. A prompt sale avoids that route, because the payoff comes out of the price.

The local market adds context. The Census Bureau counts 82,689 households in the city, and only 47.4 percent of homes are owned by their occupants (2020 to 2024), with a median owner-occupied value of $188,000. With median gross rent at $1,250, a share of sellers are landlords, and a rented house carries the same lien as any other.

faqs.q: Which office answers questions about a Fayetteville property tax bill?
faqs.a: Cumberland County Tax Administration, at 910-678-7507 or 117 Dick Street, Room 530. It handles assessment, billing and payment arrangements for Fayetteville owners.

faqs.q: When does interest begin on an unpaid Fayetteville bill?
faqs.a: January 6. The county tells owners to pay by January 5, and under state law a 2 percent charge runs to February 1, followed by three-fourths of one percent each month.

faqs.q: What combined rate applies inside Fayetteville city limits?
faqs.a: The county's 2026 rate page prints 0.9485, built from 0.4495 for the city and 0.499 for the county. Solid waste, stormwater and vehicle charges are added separately.

faqs.q: Is it too late to appeal my Fayetteville value?
faqs.a: Not for the 2027 tax year. The county lists February 5, 2027 as the informal deadline, with the Board of Equalization and Review taking formal appeals afterward. The 2026 board adjourned May 20, 2026.

faqs.q: Does the unpaid tax stay with the house after a sale?
faqs.a: Yes, the lien stays on the parcel and follows it to the buyer. Sellers usually clear it at closing through the closing attorney.
